clue.text: It eases sores in hospital cases

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words hospital cases

explanation.surface: Something that soothes the sores of patients on a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hospital cases' looks like the patients, but the word sits inside it: hospiTAL Cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft powder dusted on skin, it soothes chafing and sores.

clue.text: Loud chuckles first heard from Lewis Carroll

definitions.text: Loud chuckles first heard from Lewis Carroll

parts.words: Loud chuckles first heard from Lewis Carroll
parts.note: Lewis Carroll coined this word, blending chuckle and snort, in Through the Looking-Glass

explanation.surface: A note on the origin of a word for noisy laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful noisy laughs, a word invented by the author of the Alice books.

clue.text: Father to the French, mother to the Germans

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
au is French for 'to the'

explanation.surface: A language lesson: one word for a parent in French, another in German.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a pair of translations, but only the second half is the definition; 'Father' and 'to the French' build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: German for wife or married woman, so a mother as Germans would address her.

clue.text: Openings for a number in large towns

indicators.note: in places a and the number inside the word for large towns

parts.note: cities are large towns
V is the Roman numeral five, a number

explanation.surface: Plenty of job openings for some people in big towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollows or holes, as in a tooth, are gaps or openings.

clue.text: Habits of well bred philosophers

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, as in the old U and non-U distinction
sages are wise thinkers, philosophers

explanation.surface: The customs of upper-class thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary practices or ways of doing things are habits.

clue.text: Cook makes tarts for demanding employer

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rework them, so the letters of makes tarts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen worker baking for a boss who wants everything just so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as the person making tarts; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss who drives workers hard is a strict, demanding employer.

clue.text: Eat, but not seriously, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it is said aloud

parts.note: said in jest means not seriously

explanation.surface: Someone telling us to eat, though only joking.
explanation.definitionFit: To take food into the body is to swallow it, to eat.

clue.text: Building up runs, retaining the Ashes?

indicators.note: building up suggests constructing, so the letters of runs are rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: A cricket team piling up runs to keep the Ashes, the England-Australia test trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England v Australia test series, its trophy a small urn; here ashes are literal cremated remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels for cremated remains hold, or retain, ashes.

clue.text: Shrink from hunting initially — there's wild boar around

indicators.note: around means the jumbled boar goes round the next letter
wild suggests disorder, so the letters of boar are jumbled
initially picks the opening letter of hunting

explanation.surface: A hunter flinching because a wild boar is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns BOAR into ABOR, and 'around' puts that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to recoil or shrink from it.

clue.text: In bars, tea may be served for a teetotaller

indicators.note: served as a dish is prepared, so the letters of in bars tea are rearranged

explanation.surface: In pubs, tea might be offered to someone who does not drink alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from alcohol abstains, a synonym for a teetotaller.

clue.text: Awakening after hundred years heavy drinking

indicators.note: after places the waking word behind the letter for a century

parts.note: C is a century, a hundred years, from the Roman numeral for 100
arousing means awakening

explanation.surface: Sleeping Beauty wakes after a century and goes on a bender.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking and making merry noisily is a bout of heavy drinking.

clue.text: They go under water, coming back glossy

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: Swimmers ducking under and resurfacing shiny with water.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom spines of boats run below the waterline, under water.

clue.text: Large figures of business deficit — I closed

indicators.note: closed means the I comes at the close, at the end

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: A company owner admitting closure after big losses.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge statues, like the one at Rhodes, are large figures.

clue.text: Produce a lower type of offspring

definitions.text: Produce a lower type of offspring

parts.words: Produce a lower type of offspring
parts.note: a lower is something that lows, a cow, so this is to give birth to a young cow

explanation.surface: Having children of an inferior kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' seems to mean inferior; read it as one who lows, a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: For a cow to give birth is to bring forth its young.

clue.text: Nick has an ambition to succeed in football

parts.note: to score is to nick, make a notch
an gives the article a
a goal is an ambition

explanation.surface: A player called Nick dreams of making it as a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is a verb meaning cut a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the ball in the net is the way to succeed in a football match.

clue.text: Wreck that's broken up with little hesitation

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of that's are rearranged

parts.note: er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A wreck being broken up, with someone hesitating briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash or ruin something completely is to wreck it.

clue.text: Honours degrees?

definitions.meaning: to honour is to esteem or value highly
levels or grades, as in first-class or second-rate

explanation.surface: A question about university honours degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honours degrees' is a British university award; split it into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To value someone highly, and classes or grades of something, both fit the word.

clue.text: Look around a ship of the line

indicators.note: around means the word for look wraps the next pieces

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Inspecting a battleship that sails with the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship of the line' is a warship; here 'line' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope is a kind of line.

clue.text: Do some housework? Yes

indicators.note: some means only part of the word housework is taken

explanation.surface: A question about doing chores, answered with a cheerful yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing 'Yes' answers the question: needlework is indeed some of the housework, and some of the word housework too.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch is to do a task with needle and thread.

clue.text: Means to put on a brave face

definitions.text: Means to put on a brave face

parts.words: Means to put on a brave face
parts.note: the brave are warriors, and this colouring is literally put on their faces before battle

explanation.surface: Advice on how to appear courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on a brave face' is an idiom for hiding distress; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Colouring daubed on a warrior's face is a way to adorn a fighter's features.

clue.text: High place for a bird to live in

indicators.note: in puts the word for to live inside the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A bird looking for a lofty spot to make its home.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan plateau region, it is among the highest places on earth.

clue.text: College servant proverbially required to lie in his work?

definitions.text: College servant proverbially required to lie in his work?

parts.words: College servant proverbially required to lie in his work?
parts.note: a college servant at Oxford or Cambridge who tidies rooms; the proverb says as you make your bed so you must lie in it

explanation.surface: A college worker obliged by an old saying to rest on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge such a servant cleans students' rooms; the proverb 'as you make your bed, so you must lie in it' supplies the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaner employed at a Cambridge college to tidy rooms is a college servant.

clue.text: It's obvious I've been set back by depression

indicators.note: set back means the letters are turned round backwards

parts.note: a dent is a small depression

explanation.surface: Someone admits a slump has clearly held them back.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see means clear or obvious.

clue.text: I misdo translation of particular expressions

indicators.note: translation changes words into a new form, so the letters of I misdo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession of botching the translation of some phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrases peculiar to one language are its particular expressions.

clue.text: Two cardinals appear in this work

indicators.note: appear in puts the two points inside the word this

parts.note: E and S are two cardinal points of the compass, east and south

explanation.surface: Two senior churchmen turn up in a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen; here they are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation is a substantial piece of academic work.

clue.text: Screen has crimson centre and unusual rose edging

indicators.note: edging means the jumbled rose forms a border around the colour, which sits in the centre
unusual means the letters of rose are put in an odd order

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A decorative screen with a red middle and a rose-pattern border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' tells us the colour sits in the middle, with the jumbled flower forming its border.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental screen behind a church altar is a reredos.

clue.text: One called round, being sorry

indicators.note: round means the word for called goes round the letter

parts.note: rung means telephoned, called
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A visitor came by, apologising.
explanation.definitionFit: Regretting something is being sorry about it.

clue.text: Travel free over the Orient

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to rid is to free
E is east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Free travel across the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey on a horse or vehicle is to travel.

clue.text: Freely able to speak with added detail

indicators.note: freely means the letters of able are arranged at will

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Speaking freely and at length, with plenty of detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate or detailed things are richly worked out.

clue.text: Frank, ready to do business, …

definitions.meaning: a shop ready to trade is not closed

explanation.surface: A man named Frank ready for trade, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and also trading: both senses fit.

clue.text: … is not faster at splitting points

indicators.note: splitting means at goes between the two points, prising them apart

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Frank is no fast-goer, splitting points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' looks like quicker; it means one who fasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who consumes food is plainly not fasting.

clue.text: Curse the motherland!

parts.note: the oath is an expletive, and split in two it reads dam, a mother animal, plus nation, a land

explanation.surface: An exile's angry outburst against their home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motherland' splits into mother (DAM, a parent animal) and land (NATION).
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of anger is an oath, a curse.

clue.text: School-leaver's certificate?

parts.note: Latin for let him go out, it is permission for a boarder to leave school for a short time

explanation.surface: A query about the qualification given on leaving school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School-leaver's certificate' suggests final exams; it is a boarder's temporary leave pass in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass from a boarding school permitting a pupil a brief absence is a leaving document.
